up-01.claim: A Samajwadi Party member and former MP petitioned the Supreme Court on 28 November 2025 against the Commission's notification and the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's orders under it, ThePrint reported. The petition said the timeline was unreasonable, set unreasonable work expectations and came without practical training, and asked for a searchable database.

The Collective says it spoke to four officials; one ERO is quoted on the auto-generated form, so the claim now says 'registration officers it spoke to'. up-02.claim: The Reporters' Collective reported, from more than 4.3 lakh Form 7 disclosures on the Uttar Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer's website, that 87,127 deletion requests were filed by registration officers and assistant registration officers between 15 March and 2 April 2026 and that none of them gave a reason. Registration officers it spoke to said ERONET generated a Form 7 carrying their digital signature whenever they did not approve a voter at a hearing. It also reported that 1,10,476 deletion requests from individuals were accepted after the deadline.
up-02.response: The Collective said the Chief Electoral Officer and the Commission had not replied by publication. On 13 October 2026 IANS reported the Chief Electoral Officer's office calling the claims misleading and saying "Notices, hearings, scrutiny and recorded orders preceded action. Pending cases were decided after 6 March as per procedure."

up-27.claim: The Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh, Navdeep Rinwa, said on 30 October that each District Election Officer would be held accountable for unnecessary pending cases, inactive users, incomplete profiles, errors in the roll or lax supervision in the district, Hindustan Times and The Hindu reported. In the official statement The Hindu prints, District Election Officers are to log in to ECINET every day, and no officer is to share a user ID, password or OTP. Both reports say the receipt and disposal of Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 is to be reviewed daily and that no form is to stay pending at any level. Hindustan Times reports that a call request made through the Book a Call with BLO facility is not to stay pending for more than 48 hours, and that a booth level officer who marks a request Contacted or Unavailable without contacting the elector is to face strict action. It also reports that Rinwa sought an explanation from the present District Election Officer of Pilibhit and his predecessor over a complaint that one elector's EPIC number was shown with another elector's details in the roll of Pilibhit Sadar. An inquiry there found that 13,779 erroneous forms had been entered between 31 May and 29 August 2026 and that 10,470 of them were accepted.
